= 5 + 6 - 4

= 11 - 4

= 7

P. C. Mahalanobis is regarded as the architect of India's Five-Year Plans due to his formulation of the Mahalanobis model, which guided planned economic development with emphasis on heavy industries and long-term growth.

Key Points:

• P.C. Mahalanobis was a renowned statistician and planner.

• He played a central role in India's planning framework.

• The Mahalanobis model emphasized capital goods industries.

• It shaped the Second Five-Year Plan.

• The model focused on long-term self-reliance.

• Planning aimed at balanced industrial growth.

• Mahalanobis contributed to institution-building.

• He was associated with the Indian Statistical Institute.

• His ideas influenced public sector expansion.

• He shaped India's early development strategy.

During the Gangaur festival in Madhya Pradesh, unmarried girls perform a ritual involving a decorated earthen pot known as Ghudlia, inside which lamps are placed. The practice symbolizes devotion, marital aspirations, and prosperity, and is closely associated with regional folk traditions.

Key Points:

• Gangaur is a traditional festival associated with Goddess Gauri (Parvati).

• It is celebrated mainly by women and unmarried girls.

• In Madhya Pradesh, the ritual vessel used is called Ghudlia.

• Lamps placed inside Ghudlia symbolize auspiciousness and hope for good marriage.

• The pot is often decorated and carried in processions.

• Kalash is a general ritual pot used in many Hindu ceremonies.

• Matki is a common earthen pot without specific ritual association here.

• Deepdan refers to the act of donating lamps, not a vessel.

• Gangaur rituals vary across Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.

• The practice reflects regional adaptations of common festivals.

When an object is placed at the center of curvature (C) of a concave mirror, the reflected rays converge back at the same point. This results in an image that is real, inverted, and equal in size to the object, formed exactly at the center of curvature.

Key Points:

• A concave mirror converges parallel rays to a focal point.

• The center of curvature lies at twice the focal length.

• Rays passing through C retrace their path after reflection.

• The image is formed at C itself.

• The image is real and can be obtained on a screen.

• The image is inverted relative to the object.

• The size of the image is equal to the object size.

• This case represents a standard ray-diagram position.

• The object distance equals the image distance.

• The situation illustrates mirror symmetry in reflection.

The economic reforms initiated in 1991 in India are collectively known as the New Economic Policy (NEP). These reforms marked a shift from a state-controlled economic framework to a more market-oriented system, emphasizing efficiency, competitiveness, and global integration.

Key Points:

• The New Economic Policy (1991) introduced structural reforms in the Indian economy.

• It was built around the three pillars of Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation (LPG).

• Liberalisation reduced industrial licensing, price controls, and entry barriers.

• Privatisation expanded the role of the private sector in production and services.

• Globalisation increased trade openness and foreign investment flows.

• The Five-Year Plan framework was India's earlier model for planned economic development.

• Five-Year Plans focused on sectoral targets, public investment, and centralized planning.

• The New Fiscal Policy refers to reforms related to taxation, expenditure, and deficit management.

• Fiscal policy reforms aimed at macroeconomic stability and revenue efficiency.

• The term Economic Reconstruction Plan is used in various countries to denote post-crisis recovery strategies.

• Reconstruction plans generally focus on stabilization, restructuring, and revival.

• India's 1991 reforms combined macroeconomic stabilization with structural change.

• The NEP altered the relationship between the state, market, and global economy.

• These reforms reshaped industrial policy, trade policy, and financial regulation.

• The policy transition marked a new phase in India's economic development trajectory.

In sports, stimulants are substances that act on the central nervous system to increase alertness, concentration, and reaction time, while reducing the sensation of fatigue. Due to their performance-enhancing and health-risk potential, they are classified as prohibited substances under anti-doping regulations.

Key Points:

• Stimulants increase alertness, wakefulness, and mental focus.

• They reduce the perception of tiredness and exhaustion.

• Common examples include amphetamine, cocaine, and ephedrine.

• Stimulants can provide unfair competitive advantage.

• They pose risks such as cardiac stress and addiction.

• Anabolic agents promote muscle growth and strength, not alertness.

• Peptide hormones regulate growth, metabolism, and recovery processes.

• Beta-2 agonists are primarily used for respiratory conditions like asthma.

• Anti-doping rules prohibit stimulants in-competition.

• Athlete responsibility includes awareness of prohibited substance categories.

The Rigveda is organized into Mandalas (books), and each Mandala is further divided into Suktas, which are collections of verses composed in praise of specific Vedic deities.

Key Points:

• The Rigveda is the oldest Vedic text.

• It consists of 10 Mandalas.

• Each Mandala contains multiple Suktas (hymns).

• Suktas are composed of verses.

• Hymns are dedicated to deities like Agni, Indra, Soma.

• Kandas are divisions in later Vedic texts.

• Puranas are post-Vedic narrative texts.

• Samhita refers to the Vedic text as a whole.

• The structure reflects systematic oral composition.

• Suktas form the core liturgical units.

Aruna Asaf Ali is remembered for hoisting the national flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan on 9 August 1942 during the Quit India Movement, sustaining mass momentum after senior leaders were arrested.

Key Points:

• The Quit India Movement began in August 1942.

• Gowalia Tank Maidan (August Kranti Maidan) was the launch site.

• Aruna Asaf Ali's act symbolized civil resistance.

• She supported underground organization thereafter.

• Women assumed visible leadership roles in 1942.

• The event galvanized urban participation.

• National symbols reinforced collective resolve.

• The movement demanded immediate British withdrawal.

• Her contribution became an emblem of defiance.

• Post-Independence, she remained active in public life.

Fraternity: Constitutional Norm and Human Need examines fraternity as a crucial value that sustains democracy, equality, and social cohesion, emphasizing its role beyond legal equality and liberty.

Key Points:

• The book focuses on fraternity as a constitutional value.

• Fraternity is essential for social unity and mutual respect.

• It complements liberty and equality in democratic systems.

• The idea draws from constitutional philosophy.

• Fraternity addresses social divisions and exclusion.

• It emphasizes human dignity and solidarity.

• Economic inequality is not the book's primary theme.

• The work is normative rather than purely historical.

• It links constitutional ideals with societal ethics.

• Fraternity is presented as a human necessity for democracy.

The Montagu - Chelmsford Reforms, implemented through the Government of India Act, 1919, introduced dyarchy in provincial administration. Under this system, subjects were divided into reserved and transferred categories, administered respectively by British officials and Indian ministers.

Key Points:

• Dyarchy means dual government at the provincial level.

• Introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919.

• Based on recommendations of Montagu - Chelmsford Reforms.

• Reserved subjects included police, finance, and revenue.

• Transferred subjects included education, health, and agriculture.

• Indian ministers were responsible to provincial legislatures.

• The Indian Councils Act, 1861 expanded legislative councils only.

• Morley - Minto Reforms, 1909 introduced separate electorates.

• The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished dyarchy in provinces.

• Dyarchy marked a limited step toward self-governance.

The law of demand states that, other factors remaining constant (ceteris paribus), there is an inverse relationship between the price of a commodity and its quantity demanded. Consumers tend to buy less when prices rise and more when prices fall.

Key Points:

• The law of demand explains consumer purchasing behaviour.

• It establishes an inverse relationship between price and demand.

• Ceteris paribus means other determinants remain unchanged.

• Higher prices reduce purchasing power.

• Consumers substitute toward cheaper alternatives.

• The law applies to normal market conditions.

• It forms the basis of the downward-sloping demand curve.

• Income, tastes, and prices of substitutes are held constant.

• The law is fundamental to price determination.

• It operates in competitive markets.

The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) strengthens witness protection by allowing video conferencing and identity concealment, especially for vulnerable or threatened witnesses, ensuring safety while maintaining the integrity of judicial proceedings.

Key Points:

• BNSS modernizes criminal procedure through technology integration.

• Video conferencing reduces physical exposure of witnesses.

• Identity concealment protects witnesses from intimidation or retaliation.

• These provisions support fair and effective trials.

• Vulnerable witnesses include victims of serious crimes.

• Anonymous jury systems are not part of Indian criminal procedure.

• Recording statements via SMS is not legally recognized.

• Physical attendance may still be required where necessary.

• The provision balances witness safety and due process.

• It aligns with broader goals of justice system modernization.

The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha shortly after the Mahaparinirvana of Buddha, with the objective of preserving and compiling his teachings. It marked the beginning of the formal codification of Buddhist doctrine.

Key Points:

• The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha.

• It was convened under the patronage of King Ajatashatru.

• The council aimed to compile the Vinaya and Sutta Pitakas.

• Mahakassapa presided over the council.

• The Second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali, not Lumbini.

• The Second Council addressed disputes over monastic discipline.

• The Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra under Ashoka.

• It focused on purifying the Sangha and doctrinal unity.

• The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir under Kanishka.

• Each council played a role in the development of Buddhist traditions.

Tippani is a women-centric folk dance of Gujarat, traditionally performed during construction or agricultural activities, using a wooden tool (tippani) to create rhythmic patterns while dancing.

Key Points:

• Tippani originates in Saurashtra and Kutch regions.

• Performed mainly by women in groups.

• Uses the tippani tool for percussive rhythm.

• Reflects community labor traditions.

• Songs accompany synchronized movements.

• The dance expresses collective coordination.

• Rajasthan features forms like Ghoomar.

• Maharashtra is known for Lavani.

• Punjab is associated with Giddha.

• Tippani remains part of Gujarati cultural heritage.

After Shivaji's death in 1680, effective political power in the Maratha state gradually shifted to the Peshwas, who largely belonged to the Chitpavan Brahmana community. They became the real administrators and power brokers of the Maratha Empire.

Key Points:

• Shivaji founded the Maratha state in the 17th century.

• After his death, succession struggles weakened royal authority.

• The office of Peshwa gained increasing importance.

• Most Peshwas belonged to the Chitpavan Brahmana community.

• They exercised authority over administration and military affairs.

• The Chhatrapati became largely a ceremonial ruler.

• Mughals remained external rivals, not internal rulers.

• Deshmukhs were local revenue officials.

• Kunbis were primarily agrarian communities.

• Chitpavan dominance shaped 18th-century Maratha politics.

The Special Category State status is not a constitutional provision. It was an administrative classification granted by the National Development Council (NDC) to support states with geographical and socio-economic disadvantages.

Key Points:

• Special Category State status is not mentioned in the Constitution.

• It was conferred through decisions of the National Development Council.

• The status aimed to support hill and border states.

• Criteria included difficult terrain and low revenue capacity.

• Article 275 provides grants-in-aid but does not define special category status.

• The Inter-State Council has no constitutional role in granting this status.

• Article 280 empowers the Finance Commission, not for special category designation.

• The status affected plan assistance patterns, not legal autonomy.

• NDC functioned as a planning and coordination body.

• The concept reflects policy-based federal support mechanisms.

The Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) is published by Germanwatch in collaboration with NewClimate Institute. The index evaluates countries based on their performance in climate mitigation, renewable energy, and climate policy.

Key Points:

• The CCPI assesses national climate performance.

• It is published annually.

• Germanwatch is an environmental advocacy organization.

• NewClimate Institute focuses on climate policy analysis.

• The index covers emissions, energy use, and policy action.

• Countries are ranked based on quantitative indicators.

• It promotes transparency and accountability.

• The index supports global climate governance efforts.

• It complements scientific assessments of climate action.

• CCPI highlights progress toward climate goals.

Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa Rebellion (1922 - 24) in the Agency tracts of present-day Andhra Pradesh. The uprising was rooted in resistance to colonial forest regulations that curtailed tribal access to land, shifting cultivation, and forest produce, directly motivating the rebellion he organized.

Key Points:

• The Rampa Rebellion occurred in the Eastern Ghats region.

• Alluri Sitarama Raju emerged as a charismatic tribal leader.

• Colonial forest laws restricted customary tribal rights.

• Limits on shifting cultivation affected tribal livelihoods.

• Forced labor and policing intensified grievances.

• The movement combined local traditions with anti-colonial aims.

• Guerrilla tactics were employed in forested terrain.

• The rebellion mobilized Adivasi communities.

• It represented resistance to colonial resource control.

• The episode is significant in tribal-led freedom struggles.

Gandhara images often depict features such as halo and curly hair, which are characteristic of Graeco-Roman artistic influence. These stylistic elements entered North-West India due to sustained cultural contact with the Hellenistic world, explaining the distinctive appearance of Gandhara sculptures.

Key Points:

• Gandhara School of Art developed in North-West India.

• It flourished under Kushan patronage.

• Sculptures frequently show halo around the head.

• Curly hair resembles Greco-Roman sculptural style.

• Use of realistic anatomy and drapery is prominent.

• These features indicate Graeco-Roman influence.

• Cultural contact occurred through Indo-Greek and Roman trade links.

• Gandhara art contrasts with indigenous Mathura style.

• The halo became a lasting feature in Buddhist iconography.

• Art reflects syncretism of Indian and Western traditions.

Under official field hockey rules, goals and penalties follow precise technical conditions related to the shooting circle, penalty corners, and penalty strokes, making all three statements correct.

Key Points:

• A field goal is valid only if played from inside the shooting circle.

• Goals from outside the circle are not counted.

• During a penalty corner, the ball must exit and re-enter the circle.

• This ensures proper execution and fairness.

• A penalty stroke may be pushed or flicked.

• The ball may be lifted to any height during a penalty stroke.

• These rules are governed by the International Hockey Federation (FIH).

• Penalties aim to balance attacking opportunity and defensive safety.

• Accurate rule enforcement maintains uniform gameplay standards.

• These norms apply in international and national competitions.

Why I Am a Hindu is authored by Shashi Tharoor, where he presents a philosophical and cultural interpretation of Hinduism rooted in pluralism, inclusivity, and civilizational values.

Key Points:

• Shashi Tharoor authored Why I Am a Hindu in 2018.

• The book explores Hinduism as a cultural and civilizational idea.

• It emphasizes tolerance, diversity, and non-dogmatism.

• Pavan K. Verma authored Being Indian, focusing on Indian identity and values.

• Aravind Adiga is known for The White Tiger, a socio-economic novel.

• Gurcharan Das authored India Unbound, on post-independence economic history.

• Tharoor's work combines history, philosophy, and contemporary debate.

• The book engages with constitutional and cultural discourse.

• It distinguishes religion from political ideology.

• The work contributes to discussions on Indian pluralism.

The Indian Super League (ISL) commenced in 2014, with its inaugural match hosted in Kolkata, a city with a deep-rooted football culture. The launch marked the beginning of a franchise-based professional football league aimed at transforming the structure and visibility of football in India.

Key Points:

• The Indian Super League was launched in 2014 as a professional football league.

• The inaugural match was held in Kolkata.

• Kolkata has a long-standing tradition of football patronage and clubs.

• The opening match symbolized the formal commencement of the league.

• ISL was structured as a franchise-based competition.

• The league aimed to enhance professional standards in Indian football.

• International players and coaches were integrated into the league.

• ISL matches were organized across multiple Indian cities.

• The league contributed to commercial growth and fan engagement.

• ISL played a role in strengthening domestic football ecosystems.

Murlikant Petkar became India's first Paralympic medallist by winning a gold medal in men's 50m freestyle swimming at the 1972 Heidelberg Paralympics, marking a historic milestone in Indian para-sports.

Key Points:

• Murlikant Petkar represented India at the 1972 Paralympic Games.

• The Games were held in Heidelberg, Germany.

• He won gold in men's 50m freestyle swimming.

• This was India's first-ever Paralympic medal.

• Petkar was a war-injured soldier, reflecting resilience and determination.

• Devendra Jhajharia is a javelin thrower with multiple Paralympic golds, but from a later period.

• Mariyappan Thangavelu won high jump gold at Rio 2016, not India's first medal.

• Avani Lekhara won shooting gold at Tokyo 2020, decades later.

• Paralympic achievements highlight inclusive sporting excellence.

• Petkar's victory laid the foundation for India's Paralympic journey.

The Mahalanobis strategy emphasized channeling investment toward the capital goods sector to build domestic capacity for producing machines and infrastructure, enabling long-term self-reliant growth.

Key Points:

• The strategy underpinned India's early planning framework.

• Focus on heavy industries expanded production capacity.

• Capital goods enable growth across other sectors.

• The approach favored long-term over short-term consumption.

• It shaped priorities of the Second Five-Year Plan.

• Public sector investment played a central role.

• Industrial diversification was a key objective.

• Reduced dependence on imports was emphasized.

• The model linked investment structure to growth path.

• Planning sought balanced industrial development.

Revenue receipts of the government include income that does not create repayment obligations. These receipts arise from tax revenues and non-tax revenues, which are regular inflows meant for meeting routine expenditures, explaining the absence of financial liability.

Key Points:

• Revenue receipts form part of government income.

• They do not create future repayment obligations.

• These receipts are non-redeemable in nature.

• Tax revenue includes direct and indirect taxes.

• Non-tax revenue includes fees, fines, and dividends.

• Revenue receipts support day-to-day government expenditure.

• They differ from capital receipts, which may create liabilities.

• Regular inflows ensure fiscal continuity.

• Budget classification distinguishes revenue from capital items.

• The concept is central to public finance management.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal was inspired by which famous monument? ताजमहल किस प्रसिद्ध स्मारक से प्रेरित था?
questions.solution:
The Taj Mahal represents the culmination of the Mughal architectural tradition, drawing significant inspiration from Humayun's Tomb, which pioneered the use of a grand garden-tomb (charbagh) layout, symmetrical design, and monumental scale in Indo-Islamic architecture.

Key Points:

• Humayun's Tomb is regarded as the architectural precursor to the Taj Mahal.

• It was built in Delhi during the reign of the early Mughal dynasty.

• The tomb introduced the charbagh (four-part garden) concept in India.

• Emphasis on symmetry and axial planning influenced later Mughal monuments.

• The Taj Mahal refined these elements using white marble and intricate inlay work.

• Jama Masjid is primarily a congregational mosque, not a funerary monument.

• Jama Masjid emphasizes open courtyards and prayer spaces, not garden-tomb design.

• Victoria Memorial reflects Indo-Saracenic colonial architecture, built during British rule.

• Its style and purpose differ from Mughal imperial tomb architecture.

• Qutub Minar is a victory tower/minaret, unrelated to tomb architecture.

• Qutub Minar belongs to the early Delhi Sultanate period, not Mughal aesthetics.

• The Taj Mahal represents the mature phase of Mughal architectural evolution.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: Red herring
questions.questionHtml:

Red herring

options.text: A false clue meant to mislead
options.html: A false clue meant to mislead

The idiom refers to deliberate distraction intended to divert attention from the real issue.

Why the other options are incorrect

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful passage: 1) Marine ecosystems are sensitive to temperature shifts. 2. Coral bleaching is one visible consequence. 3. Rising ocean temperatures disrupt symbiotic algae. 4. This affects reef biodiversity and fisheries.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful passage:

1) Marine ecosystems are sensitive to temperature shifts. 2. Coral bleaching is one visible consequence. 3. Rising ocean temperatures disrupt symbiotic algae. 4. This affects reef biodiversity and fisheries.
questions.solution:
The passage follows a clear general statement → cause → effect → consequence sequence.

Sentence 1 is the appropriate opening sentence as it introduces the general idea that marine ecosystems are sensitive to temperature changes, without any referential dependency.

Sentence 3 logically follows by explaining the cause - rising ocean temperatures disrupting symbiotic algae.

Sentence 2 then presents a specific, observable effect, namely coral bleaching, which results from the disruption mentioned earlier.

Sentence 4 works as the concluding sentence, where "This" refers to coral bleaching and explains its broader impact on reef biodiversity and fisheries.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) 3-2-1-4 - begins with a cause before introducing the general context.

2) 3-2-4-1 - places the general statement at the end, breaking coherence.

4) 1-2-3-4 - introduces the effect before explaining the cause.

Final correct sequence:

1 → 3 → 2 → 4

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage. 1) Regular check-ups are essential to detect issues early. 2) Maintaining good dental hygiene is crucial. 3) It prevents cavities, gum disease, and other oral problems. 4) Brushing and flossing daily form the core of this practice.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage.

1) Regular check-ups are essential to detect issues early.

2) Maintaining good dental hygiene is crucial.

3) It prevents cavities, gum disease, and other oral problems.

4) Brushing and flossing daily form the core of this practice.
questions.solution:
The passage follows a clear general statement → benefit → method → supporting measure sequence.

Sentence 2 is the correct opening sentence because it introduces the central idea - the importance of maintaining good dental hygiene - without any reference to prior information.

Sentence 3 logically follows by explaining why dental hygiene is crucial, listing the benefits it provides (prevention of cavities and gum disease).

Sentence 4 then specifies how this hygiene is maintained, with "this practice" clearly referring back to maintaining good dental hygiene.

Sentence 1 appropriately concludes the passage by adding a complementary measure - regular check-ups - that supports the overall goal of oral health.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) 2-1-3-4 - introduces check-ups before explaining daily hygiene practices.

2) 2-4-3-1 - places the method before stating the benefits, weakening logical flow.

3) 3-4-2-1 - begins with benefits without introducing the core topic.

Final correct sequence:

2 → 3 → 4 → 1

questions.question: Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure: It had been made clear by the committee that the rule would not be altered.
questions.questionHtml:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

It had been made clear by the committee that the rule would not be altered.

options.text: The committee made it clear that the rule would not be altered.
options.html: The committee made it clear that the rule would not be altered.

options.text: The rule was made clear not to be altered by the committee.
options.html: The rule was made clear not to be altered by the committee.

options.text: The rule alteration was clarified by the committee.
options.html: The rule alteration was clarified by the committee.

options.text: The committee had altered the rule as made clear.
options.html: The committee had altered the rule as made clear.

questions.solution:
Tense

Past perfect passive → Past simple active (reporting verb)

Structure

Passive: It + had been + past participle + by + agent + that-clause

Active: Agent + past simple verb + object + that-clause

Why the correct option is right

Option (1) correctly:

· Restores the real agent ("the committee") as the subject,

· Converts "had been made clear" to "made it clear",

· Preserves the meaning, intent, and reporting structure of the original sentence.

Why the other options are incorrect

2) Retains passive structure and is syntactically awkward.

3) Changes meaning and removes the reporting emphasis.

4) Introduces an incorrect action ("altered the rule") not stated in the original.

Correct Active:

The committee made it clear that the rule would not be altered.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word. The ________ theory revolutionized the field of anthropology.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.

The ________ theory revolutionized the field of anthropology.
questions.solution:
Evolutionary is the correct spelling, referring to theories based on gradual development and change over time, which fits the context of anthropology.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) evoluttionary - incorrect double t.

3) evoulusionary - incorrect vowel sequence and root distortion.

4) evvolutionary - incorrect consonant doubling.

Other confusing spellings (Correct vs Incorrect)

revolutionary vs revoluttionary

evolution vs evoloution

theoretical vs theorotical

anthropology vs anthropolgy

Usage example:

The evolutionary theory reshaped anthropology, unlike creationist explanations that reject gradual change.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) Idea - not idiomatic in this context.

2) Belief - does not collocate naturally with responsibility.

4) View - inappropriate for personal obligation.

Corrected sentence:

She has a strong sense of responsibility.

questions.question: Select the correct option: The manuscript was replete with obscure references, many of __ baffled reviewers.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct option:

The manuscript was replete with obscure references, many of __ baffled reviewers.
questions.solution:
Which is used to refer to things (references) in a non-defining relative clause.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) Whom - used for people, not things.

3) Them - cannot introduce a relative clause.

4) Those - demonstrative, grammatically incorrect here.

Corrected sentence:

The manuscript was replete with obscure references, many of which baffled reviewers.

questions.question: Change the following from active to passive: Someone had left the emergency exit unlocked overnight.
questions.questionHtml:
Change the following from active to passive:

Someone had left the emergency exit unlocked overnight.

options.text: The emergency exit had been left unlocked overnight.
options.html: The emergency exit had been left unlocked overnight.

options.text: The emergency exit was being left unlocked overnight.
options.html: The emergency exit was being left unlocked overnight.

options.text: The emergency exit had to be left unlocked overnight.
options.html: The emergency exit had to be left unlocked overnight.

options.text: The emergency exit has been left unlocked overnight.
options.html: The emergency exit has been left unlocked overnight.

questions.solution:
Tense

Past perfect (active) → Past perfect (passive)

Structure

Active: Subject + had + past participle + object

Passive: Object + had been + past participle

Why the correct option is right

Option (1) correctly:

· Shifts the object ("the emergency exit") to the subject position,

· Converts had left to had been left,

· Retains the past perfect tense and the time expression "overnight."

Why the other options are incorrect

2) Uses past continuous passive, changing the tense.

3) Introduces obligation ("had to"), which is not present in the original sentence.

4) Uses present perfect, altering the time reference.

Correct Passive:

The emergency exit had been left unlocked overnight.

questions.question: A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech. The teacher said, "Who can solve this question?"

questions.solution:
For wh-questions in indirect speech:

· said → asked,

· Question form → statement order,

· can → could (tense backshift),

· this → that (change of deixis).

Option (1) correctly applies all these rules.

Why the other options are incorrect

2) Fails to apply tense backshift.

3) Uses incorrect reporting verb and deixis.

4) Loses the interrogative structure entirely.

Correct Indirect:

The teacher asked who could solve that question.

questions.question: A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech. The director noted that the figures had been inflated.
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

The director noted that the figures had been inflated.

options.text: The director said, "These figures have been inflated."
options.html: The director said, "These figures have been inflated."

options.text: The director said, "The figures are inflated."
options.html: The director said, "The figures are inflated."

options.text: The director said, "The figures were exaggerated."
options.html: The director said, "The figures were exaggerated."

options.text: The director said, "They inflated the figures."
options.html: The director said, "They inflated the figures."

questions.solution:
In indirect speech, past perfect ("had been inflated") is often used due to backshift after a past reporting verb. When converting to direct speech, the tense can be restored to present perfect if the situation remains relevant.

Option (1) correctly:

· Removes that,

· Restores tense to have been inflated,

· Preserves meaning and formality.

Why the other options are incorrect

2) are inflated - changes aspect and weakens evidential emphasis.

3) were exaggerated - alters wording and meaning.

4) They inflated the figures - changes voice and focus.

Correct Direct:

The director said, "These figures have been inflated."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (1) : (MEMORY BASED)
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (1): (MEMORY BASED)
questions.solution:

Contextual justification:

The sentence makes a present-tense definitional statement, so "is" is the correct linking verb.

Why other options are wrong:

2) were - past tense; context is present and general.

3) are - plural verb; incorrect for singular subject.

Corrected sentence (relevant part):

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (2) : (MEMORY BASED)

The clause expresses an evolving inevitability in the present context.

Why other options are wrong:

1) making - participle; breaks sentence structure.

4) had becoming - grammatically invalid construction.

Corrected sentence (relevant part):

questions.question: Choose the correct conditional mood. (3)

questions.question: The word "nascent" most nearly means : (4). (MEMORY BASED)

questions.question: 'The word tempering' most nearly means: (5)

4) Glorifying excessively - opposite sense.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The symposium on autonomous systems (1)/ underscored an urgent need of robust ethical frameworks (2)/ to anticipate unforeseen consequences (3)/ of machine decision-making. (4)/
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The symposium on autonomous systems (1)/ underscored an urgent need of robust ethical frameworks (2)/ to anticipate unforeseen consequences (3)/ of machine decision-making. (4)/
questions.solution:
The error lies in "an urgent need of robust ethical frameworks."

The noun need is followed by the preposition for, not of.

Why the other parts are correct

1) Correct subject phrase.

3) Correct infinitive of purpose.

4) Correct prepositional phrase.

Corrected sentence:

The symposium on autonomous systems underscored an urgent need for robust ethical frameworks to anticipate unforeseen consequences of machine decision-making.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: Only after the final audit report was submitted (1)/ did the committee realise (2)/ that the estimates, although well-documented, (3)/ has omitted indirect liabilities.(4)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

Only after the final audit report was submitted (1)/ did the committee realise (2)/ that the estimates, although well-documented, (3)/ has omitted indirect liabilities.(4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in "has omitted indirect liabilities."

There is a subject - verb agreement and tense consistency error. The subject "the estimates" is plural, and the verb must agree with it. Additionally, the reporting context is in the past, so present perfect is inappropriate.

"Has omitted" is singular and present perfect, whereas it should be plural and past perfect/simple past in keeping with the sentence structure.

Why the other parts are correct

1) Correct use of inversion after "Only after".

2) Correct past tense verb realised.

3) Correct concessive clause structure.

Corrected sentence:

Only after the final audit report was submitted did the committee realise that the estimates, although well-documented, had omitted indirect liabilities.

questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: The child cried as if he was in pain.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The child cried as if he was in pain.

options.text: as though he is in pain
options.html: as though he is in pain

options.text: as if he were in pain
options.html: as if he were in pain

questions.solution:
After as if / as though to express an unreal or hypothetical situation, formal English uses the subjunctive "were" (irrespective of the subject). The sentence implies the child was not actually in pain but behaved as though he was.

Why the other options are incorrect

1) as though he is in pain - present tense removes the sense of unreality.

3) like he was in pain - informal and grammatically weak for exam usage.

4) as he was in pain - states a real cause, changing the meaning.

Corrected sentence:

The child cried as if he were in pain.
